criteria.criterion: A new test in crates/athena-core/src/run/tests.rs has main's tip as a squash commit that is not the base's content commit but has the same governed-content fingerprint, with a green CI run on main for that tip. It asserts the baseline has reused_from set to the run address, all checks are reused and passed, baseline_ran is false, and the host read was for the squash SHA on branch main. Run `cargo test -p athena-core baseline_reused`.
criteria.evidence: baseline_reused_from_a_squash_on_main_with_the_bases_fingerprint builds main's tip as an empty commit on top of the head and points origin/main at it, then resets the head, so the tip is a different commit with the same content. CI replies Green only for (tip, main). The test asserts base_commit != tip, reused_from == CI_RUN_ADDRESS, every check is reused and passed, !baseline_ran, and a read containing head_sha={tip} and branch=main&. Ran: 3 passed, including this test.

criteria.criterion: A new test has main's tip with a different governed-content fingerprint, even if it has a green run. It asserts the baseline runs locally (baseline_ran true, reused_from None) and the output line gives the fingerprint-mismatch reason. Run `cargo test -p athena-core baseline_runs_locally`.
criteria.evidence: baseline_runs_locally_when_main_tip_has_other_governed_content gives main's tip a changed file and a Green reply. It asserts baseline_ran, reused_from None, no reused checks, no read of the tip, and exactly one 'ci         baseline runs locally: ' line containing 'has other governed content than the base'. Ran: 2 passed.

criteria.criterion: In crates/athena-core/src/run/checks.rs, the default-branch step of reused_baseline no longer passes the base's own content commit to green_run on the default branch. It passes main's commit chosen by matching fingerprint with the base's, and the doc comment of reused_baseline describes this.
criteria.evidence: checks.rs:512-527 now rev-parses refs/remotes/origin/{branch}. It calls green_run(&route, &tip, &[], &branch) only when fingerprint(&self.git, &tip, &tip) == own, and otherwise pushes a reason. `content` is no longer passed on that path. Doc item 2 (lines 457-460) describes the tip lookup by fingerprint. One stale sentence remains at lines 448-449 (minor finding).

criteria.criterion: `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean, and the change touches only the reuse path, so the landed-candidate path and the local fallback are unchanged.
criteria.evidence: Both passed in Athena's records for CI run 41892229021. The diff in checks.rs touches only the default-branch match arm and doc item 2. Step 1 (landed_job/green_run on the CI branch), content_commit, green_run and the Err fallback are unchanged (git diff HEAD~1).

findings.summary: Only main's tip is checked. The accepted reading allowed a capped walk back over main's history, which this change does not do.
findings.evidence: The reading's assumption says 'main's tip first, then a bounded walk back over its first-parent ancestors (a small cap)'. The candidate rev-parses origin/<branch> and compares only that commit. If main has moved past the base (another landing since the base was taken), no match is found and the baseline runs locally. The request's main case (the tip is the squash of the base's content) is handled, and every criterion tests only the tip. A capped first-parent walk calling green_run on the first commit whose fingerprint matches would cover the remaining case.

findings.summary: A doc sentence of reused_baseline still says the commit looked up is the base's content commit, which is now true only for step 1.
findings.evidence: 'The commit looked up is the base's content commit ([`Athena::content_commit`]): the base, or the commit under the job's own records commits, which is the one the host has.' This is left above the numbered list, and it contradicts the new item 2.

summary: The change fixes the cause of the bug. The default-branch step of reused_baseline used to look up the base's own content commit, which the host has never seen. It now reads main's tip from the local refs/remotes/origin/<branch> ref and calls green_run on that tip only when the tip's governed-content fingerprint equals the base's. If the fingerprint differs or the tip is unknown, it gives a reason and the baseline runs locally. The landed-candidate step and the local fallback are unchanged. I ran the targeted tests: the new squash-on-main test, the new mismatch test, the existing baseline tests and all ci_reuse_* tests pass. fmt, clippy and the full test suite passed in Athena's recorded CI run. The new reuse test would fail on the base, because the old code asked for a different SHA. The mismatch test would also fail there, because the old reason text lacks "than the base". All changed files are on the deliverables list. I found two minor issues. First, only main's tip is checked. The accepted reading allowed a short, capped walk back over main's history, so a base that main has already moved past still runs locally. Second, one doc sentence above the numbered steps still says the commit looked up is the base's content commit.
